scene: 2 — Inbound supply, in the calendar they plan in
detail: Four of the five specifics in scene 2's narration are falsified by the artifact on screen. (1) 'Next Tuesday at Monguno' — as of Jul 28 the next Tuesday is Aug 4, whose only cell belongs to GWOZA; Monguno's single cell in the week is SUN, AUG 2. (2) 'needs eight hundred cartons for the children booked in' — the string never appears in the page text; Monguno's cell reads 532 (children booked) over '840 on hand', and 800 is a loose round of 840, i.e. the SUPPLY figure, the opposite quantity from the one the sentence names. (3) 'the consignment covering it is on the road' — no in-transit, ETA or shipment-status element exists anywhere in the viewport or the page text; Monguno's cell carries no '+N' inbound marker at all (only Askira '38 on hand +94' and Biu '0 on hand +141' do, and both are off the top of the frame). (4) 'The Thursday distribution at Kukawa reads as at risk' — Kukawa's Thursday cell is 235 booked against 375 on hand, and its fill is byte-identical to every covered cell in the grid. The two rows that genuinely render at-risk (Askira, amber) and uncovered (Biu, red) are not in scene 2's frame at all. The judge sampled cell fills with PIL to confirm zero colour variation in the viewport.
fix_recommendation: Either renarrate the beat against the cells that exist — 'Sunday at Monguno, five hundred and thirty-two children booked in against eight hundred and forty cartons' — and drop the 'on the road' clause until an in-transit state is surfaced on this screen; OR reshape the seeded week so a genuinely at-risk and a genuinely uncovered distribution fall inside the visible seven days and the narration's named sites carry them. Do not ship the current pairing: every named fact except the site name and one weekday is wrong.

scene: 2 — Inbound supply, in the calendar they plan in
detail: The scene's concept is cover state per site AND date, and the captured frame carries neither. The scroll target was the calendar card's .method-note (its footnote), which pushed the date header row (SITE / FRI, JUL 31 ... THU, AUG 6), the card title and the card's explanatory subtitle above the fold — so the frame opens on an unlabelled grid of two-number boxes and a viewer cannot tell which day any cell belongs to. Every visible cell renders the identical covered green, so the three-state read the card exists to demonstrate is absent from its own scene. The eye is pulled instead to the 'Weeks of cover' table below, which holds the only saturated colour in the frame — so the five-second takeaway is 'the sites below are in trouble, the grid above is fine', roughly the inverse of the narration.
fix_recommendation: Make the calendar self-describing without its footnote: make the date header row sticky within the card's own scroll container, label the two numbers in-cell ('532 children booked' / '840 cartons on hand') rather than in a paragraph below the grid, and add a compact per-cell state chip ('Covered' / 'At risk' / 'Uncovered') so the state is readable as text and not only as a fill.

scene: 2 — Inbound supply, in the calendar they plan in
detail: The load-bearing encoding is effectively invisible. The covered cell fill measures #E9F3F0 against a #FFFFFF card — roughly 1.03:1 — so at projector distance the calendar reads as white boxes with an outline and the cover state, the entire point of the card, does not survive the room the audience is in. Colour-blind viewers get nothing either, since state is carried by fill alone. Compounding it in the same frame: one column stacks five identical filled primary 'Raise a shortfall' buttons beside one inert grey 'Raised Jul 24, 2026' text cell (inconsistent control styling within a single scene), Konduga's row is clipped mid-cell at the top edge and Mafa's is cut through a button at the bottom, and roughly 470px of dead white gutter runs down the left third of the frame below the sidebar card.
fix_recommendation: Raise the cover state above the visibility floor: replace the near-white tint with a saturated 4px left status bar plus a text state chip per cell, so state is legible at projector distance and without relying on colour. Normalise the shortfall column to a single control style — secondary 'Raise a shortfall' on actionable rows and a matching secondary 'View shortfall' on already-raised rows — so the column reads as one control rather than five primaries beside a dead text cell.

scene: 2 — Inbound supply, in the calendar they plan in
detail: Fits-but-mis-framed. The calendar demonstrably fits one 720px viewport (11 rows at ~51px plus header and legend is roughly 640px), but the scene scrolled to css:.card:has-text('Distribution calendar') .method-note — the footnote BELOW the grid — which pushed the date headers, the card title and the only two informative cells (amber Askira, red Biu) above the fold, clipped Konduga's row mid-cell, and handed roughly 45% of the frame to the next card while the voiceover talks about the calendar. The recipe's own note shows this was a deliberate correction for an earlier no-op scroll; it over-corrected past the subject. Both actions returned ok:true — the trace is clean, the framing is the defect.
fix_recommendation: Change the scroll target from css:.card:has-text('Distribution calendar') .method-note to the calendar table's head — css:.card:has-text('Distribution calendar') thead with block:'start' — or to the card element itself, so the date header row and all eleven site rows are settled in frame before the voiceover names a day. Keep the 2.4s hold after the settle; if the legend must also be on camera, add a second short scroll_to .method-note beat AFTER the day is named rather than opening on it.

detail: The underlying use is real and at genuine scale — eleven sites, a 0-to-5.5-week cover ladder, a live shortfall with a named deadline, a batch resolving to 657 children fed — and no skeptic would call it a toy. But two independent judges fired the same deduction rule from opposite ends. The demonstrated week contains ZERO non-covered cells inside the narrated viewport and exactly one distribution per site laid out on a perfect alphabetical diagonal, so the calendar never has to discriminate anything on camera: a skeptic sees a grid that has only ever said yes. And the shortfall's payoff — the centre actually responding — is explicitly deferred to another narrative ('What OES does with it is the next narrative'), so the loop the concept is built on never closes on screen.
fix_recommendation: Reshape what is demonstrated so the three-state read does load-bearing work on camera: put at least one genuinely at-risk and one genuinely uncovered distribution INSIDE the visible seven-day window, give at least two sites more than one distribution in the week so days collide and the grid stops reading as generated, and make the narrated Monguno/Kukawa cells the ones that carry the contrast. Separately, consider extending scene 5 to land on the OES queue with Zara's item visible in rank position, so the raise and its consequence are not separated across narratives.

scene: 5 — Zara raises a shortfall, and the centre answers
detail: The iteration's two new fields landed and are visible: CARTONS SHORT 94 and a REPORTED BY badge reading 'Komadugu Health Initiative', alongside SITE, RAISED date and NEEDED BY — so 'marked as raised by Komadugu rather than derived centrally' is now genuinely evidenced. The other half of the claim is not. 'It lands in the OES command centre ranked against every other exception by the children behind it' has no on-screen referent: no rank, no queue position, no acknowledgement, no destination link. The record's only status is an amber 'open' pill identical to the pre-existing Askira row. The claim IS stated in prose — as modal copy (tab_partner.jsx:379-382) and a toast string — but prose is not evidence. Sharper still, the card's own lede reads 'Reported upward from this screen, and answered against the same record' while sitting directly above two rows both stamped 'open', and the scene is titled 'Zara raises a shortfall, and the centre answers'. Also unevidenced: the justification Zara types on camera ('Admissions above plan for three weeks since the Baga road reopened...') is captured and then rendered nowhere on the resulting record.
fix_recommendation: Make the destination a state rather than a sentence. ShortfallSignal.resolved_by_action already exists on the model (models/demand.py:139) and rides the wire as resolved_by_action_id (serializers/demand.py:72) but is never rendered and never seeded. Seed the Askira Jul 24 signal as answered by a SupplyAction and render the actor, effect and date on that row, and add an acknowledged state between open and answered so arrival at the centre is visible. Until that exists, change the card lede to describe what the card actually shows ('Reported upward from this screen. Both awaiting an answer from OES.') and either show the rank on this screen or let the ranking sentence belong to the OES narrative that can demonstrate it. Also render the submitted note on the record so the field filled on camera is visibly retained.

scene: 5 — Zara raises a shortfall, and the centre answers
detail: Two framing misses in the scene's closing beats. The scripted punchline — Kukawa's cover row converting from a button to a dated 'Raised Jul 28, 2026' stamp, proving a duplicate raise is structurally impossible — is scrolled off the top of the final frame; the only three cover rows in frame (Ngala, Gwoza, Dikwa) all still read 'Raise a shortfall', which visually contradicts the beat. And the final scroll target, css:.card:has-text('Shortfalls you have raised') tr:last-child, resolves in a newest-first table to the OLD Askira Jul 24 row — so the camera's last gesture points at the record the demo did NOT just create. Action fidelity itself is clean: the click, fill and 'Raise it' click all returned ok:true and the toast wait succeeded, so the act genuinely happened.
fix_recommendation: Three scripting changes. (1) Replace the final scroll_to tr:last-child with scroll_to "css:.card:has-text('Shortfalls you have raised') tr:has-text('Kukawa Nutrition Centre')" so the camera lands on the row just created. (2) Insert an explicit beat between the toast and the shortfall card — scroll_to "css:tr:has-text('Kukawa Nutrition Centre')" within 'Weeks of cover by site' plus a 2.0s hold — so the viewer sees the button replaced by the dated stamp while that line is spoken. (3) End the scene with the shortfalls card top-aligned so the unrelated batch table stays out of frame.

scene: 4 — The storekeeper counts it, and the short count is evidence
detail: The scene's punchline is off-screen. The narration ends on 'it is labelled as hand-keyed, because it was', but the row carrying that label — SHP-2026-0909, Monguno, 900 cartons, 'Entered by hand', 'Counted · 60 short' — is scrolled above the viewport, along with the REPORTED BY column header that would explain what the badges mean. The 'Entered by hand' and 'Despatch advice' pills that ARE in frame therefore sit in an unlabelled column and belong to other consignments, so a cold viewer sees yellow and blue pills with no idea what dimension they encode and no way to connect them to the 900/840/60 row the scene is about. Compounding it, the 'Short counts you have raised' card itself carries no provenance at all — its five columns are CONSIGNMENT / ADVISED / YOU COUNTED / SHORT / CHILDREN AFFECTED, with no reported-by, no counter, no timestamp and no site — so the card whose whole thesis is 'this is evidence because of who recorded it and where' records none of that.
fix_recommendation: Re-script as two beats: scroll_to the SHP-2026-0909 ROW (not the card) and hold ~2.5s over 'Monguno · 900 cartons · Entered by hand · Delivered · Counted · 60 short' with the REPORTED BY header still in frame while the 'labelled as hand-keyed' line is spoken, then scroll_to the short-counts card for the children-affected line. Better still, fix it in the product so the claim is demonstrable wherever the scene is framed: put the site name, the provenance chip and the counted timestamp directly on the short-count row, so a viewer can complete the sentence 'this shortfall was counted by hand at Monguno on <date>' from that card alone.

scene: 6 — From a batch to the child who recovered
detail: The walkthrough's payoff is rendered at a scale that cannot carry it. The MUAC series occupies roughly x=575 to x=795 — about 220px, ~17% of the frame — while 35-40% of the modal's width is dead whitespace on either side of it. The two threshold labels ('125 mm · recovered', '115 mm · severe') render at roughly 7px and exist on ONE row of 33; there is no y-axis, no tick marks and no x-axis on any row, so the narration's 'climbs across their visits' has no time reference on screen and '7 visits over 6 weeks' is prose standing in for an axis. Non-highlighted rows carry zero axis reference, and their band proportions appear to differ row to row, which would mean the small multiples are not on a shared y-scale — with no axis a reader cannot check, so the rows cannot safely be compared, which is the entire purpose of a small-multiples column. The fifth record (DIK-2607-003) is sliced horizontally by the modal footer bar with its chart bleeding underneath and the green Close button sitting on top of the content region — a frame element occluding content, which is the harder of the two deduction rules that fire here — and there is no scrollbar, fade or count signposting the other 28 rows, so the modal's own '33 children' claim cannot be verified on screen. Separately the primary green Close button reuses the legend's 'Recovered' green for a dismiss action and is the highest-contrast element in the modal, and the scrim does not cover the top header bar or the orange 'open' pill behind it. Root cause of the sizing confirmed in source: .muac-spark is width:100%/height:56px (css/06-visualisation.css:318) while the SVG carries a viewBox with default preserveAspectRatio, so it scales to fit its height and letterboxes horizontally.
fix_recommendation: Product change, never a capture zoom or crop. Add preserveAspectRatio="none" (or match the viewBox ratio to the rendered box) so the series fills its column. Render the selected child as a full-width hero detail panel pinned above the cohort list, with a labelled visit axis across the six weeks and y-ticks at 115/125/135 mm at body type rather than 7px. In the cohort list, collapse the ~250px whitespace either side of each sparkline, label the shared y-scale once at the head of the chart column, and pin all rows to that one domain so they are comparable. Wrap the list in a scroll container with a persistent count ('33 treatment records') and a bottom fade so no row is hard-clipped. Restyle Close as a neutral/secondary control so green stays semantically reserved for 'Recovered', and extend the scrim over the top header bar.

detail: The walkthrough's climactic traceability claim — 'Each distribution resolves to the batch that supplied it' — resolves to shipments the partner never received. seed_distribution_records (demo/demand.py:493-525) selects the first six delivered ShipmentLines GLOBALLY and round-robins them across all eleven sites, dating each TODAY-21-index. Three visible consequences. (1) Every distribution references SHP-2026-0101/0102/0103/0201/0301/0302, whereas every consignment on the partner's own Receiving tab is SHP-2026-09xx — two disjoint series, so the batch table cannot be reconciled against the receiving record it claims to extend. (2) Every distribution (Jun 27 - Jul 7) predates every partner receipt (Jul 11 - Jul 21), at every site. (3) Biu — which is deliberately given no delivered consignment, so it correctly reads '0 cartons · awaiting first consignment' in the cover table and drives the '0 wk Thinnest cover' headline in scene 1 — nevertheless shows 'Jul 6, 2026 · Biu Nutrition Centre · LOT2601A · 280 children served' two cards below on the same page. children_served is also rng.randint(120, 340), unrelated to each site's caseload, so Ngala serves 1,761/month but distributed 166 while Askira serves 271/month and distributed 320 in a single day.
fix_recommendation: Seed distribution records from the partner's OWN delivered SHP-2026-09xx consignments rather than the first six global ShipmentLines, date each one AFTER its consignment's arrival, skip sites with no delivered receipt (which removes the Biu contradiction outright), and size children_served from the site's own weekly burn rather than a uniform random draw. The existing test asserts each record traces to 'a real delivered batch', which passes today while the batch is one the site never received — tighten it to assert the batch was delivered TO THAT SITE and before the distribution date.

detail: The calendar tells the user how to read it and then renders something that rule cannot produce. The legend states a BINARY test — 'a cell is short exactly when the second number is below the first' — and then names three colours ('Green is covered, amber at risk, red uncovered'), with no threshold given for the amber band. It is also ambiguous about its own operands: the cell renders three numbers ('38 on hand +94') while the server decides state from the on-hand figure ALONE, with cartons_inbound explicitly excluded because a truck arriving later does not cover this day (serializers/demand.py:33-45). Two independent judges each tried to reproduce the encoding from the stated rule and each concluded it predicted the wrong colours — one reading '38 +94' as 132 and deriving 'covered' for a cell that renders amber. The '+94' is never explained on screen. Related: the KPI 'Distributions not covered: 4' counts all 22 seeded plans while the grid slices to the first 7 distinct days, so only 2 non-covered cells are ever visible and the headline cannot be reconciled against the grid beneath it.
fix_recommendation: Restate the legend as the three-way rule the code actually implements and label the operands so the comparison is unambiguous — cell reads '63 booked · 38 on hand · +94 scheduled', legend reads 'green = covered by stock on hand; amber = covered only if the scheduled consignment lands; red = uncovered even with scheduled consignments'. Either scope the 'Distributions not covered' tile to the days the grid displays, or label it with its own horizon ('next 14 days') so the number has a visible denominator.

scene: 3 — Weeks of cover, and the date it runs dry
detail: Alarm-colouring beyond the stated rule. The card's subhead states two thresholds — 'At four weeks you plan; at one you triage' — but the badge bands are implemented at 2 and 4 (tab_partner.jsx:112-114), so Kukawa and Monguno at 1.6 weeks are painted triage-red when the stated triage line is 1.0, and there is no legend anywhere defining the bands. Colour is encoding an unstated rule rather than the stated one. Secondary notes in the same frame: ten identical filled dark-green 'Raise a shortfall' buttons form the heaviest column in the frame and outweigh the weeks-of-cover badges the card exists to show, with Dikwa at 5.5 weeks shouting exactly as loudly as Kukawa at 11 days; the badge column mixes bare integers (0, 2, 3, 4) with one-decimal values (0.6, 1.6, 2.5) so it does not scan; and Askira's 'Raised Jul 24, 2026' state is low-contrast grey with no status word and no link to the record, so the second-worst site reads as the one row needing no attention. The underlying arithmetic is exact — all eleven rows reconcile against on_hand / (children_per_month x 7/30), and 'Kukawa is eleven days out' verifies both on screen and by computation.
fix_recommendation: Bind the badge bands to the thresholds the card states — red below 1 week, amber 1 to 4, green at 4 and above — and put the band definition in an info bubble on the WEEKS OF COVER header rather than leaving it inferred from fills. Demote the row action to a secondary control so it sits below the measure in the hierarchy, render the badge to one fixed decimal, and raise the 'Raised ...' state to a status chip at body contrast that links to its shortfall record.

scene: 1 — The organisation that feeds the children sees the least
detail: The opening frame's dominant object is a 7-column by 11-row grid in which only 11 of 77 cells carry data — roughly 86% empty bordered boxes, with one lone populated cell per row marching diagonally down. A cold viewer's five-second read is 'there isn't much data here', which is the inverse of the scene's own claim that this organisation knows its caseload to the child. The four key figures that ARE the scene's argument (11 feeding sites, 4 distributions not covered, 0 wk thinnest cover, 1 shortfall raised) read cleanly and the role pill, org name and synthetic-environment marker all ground it properly. Secondary: the calendar's colour key sits below the table and off this viewport, so the frame shows semantic colour with no key anywhere on screen; and 'Borno', which the narration names, appears nowhere on the page.
fix_recommendation: Either collapse the calendar to only the days that carry a distribution (or render it as a per-site strip) so the ink maps to the data, or place 'Weeks of cover by site' directly under the key figures and above the calendar so the first artifact a supply lead lands on is the eleven-site cover ladder that actually carries the concept. Move the colour key inline into the calendar card's header as a compact swatch legend. Add a geography label ('Borno State, Nigeria') beside the org name so the one proper noun the narration names is checkable from the frame. Do not add a headline takeaway — this is an evidence product.

scene: 4 — The storekeeper counts it, and the short count is evidence
detail: The concept's stated novelty is the capture act — spine S3 calls a partner storekeeper with a phone 'the realistic capture device' — but the walkthrough only ever shows the READ side. The 'Record the count' affordance is on screen eight times and is never exercised; the one counted consignment simply pre-exists. Nothing on screen grounds 'records the receipt from a phone' either: this is a desktop web table with no mobile capture affordance and no 'recorded via mobile' marker anywhere. (Scored 3 rather than the dispatched judge's 2: the narration's subject is 'the storekeeper', describing off-camera how the record came to exist, so it does not claim the demo performs the capture — the action-fidelity rule is not cleanly triggered. The gap is real but softer than a contradiction.) Separately, the page's own data undercuts its premise: ten consignments were delivered Jul 11-21 and as of Jul 28 exactly one has been counted, so a screen arguing that receipt-counting is the disciplined norm shows that nine times out of ten, over 7-17 days, nobody did it.
fix_recommendation: Add an effecting beat to the scene — click 'Record the count' on a delivered consignment, show the count entry form, enter the counted figure against the advice and submit — so the discrepancy is seen being created rather than found already created. If the capture surface is desktop-only, that is itself the finding worth acting on, since the concept's low-tech tier currently has no implementation on camera. Separately, reduce the uncounted backlog in the seed so the screen's data supports rather than undercuts its own argument.

scene: 5 — Zara raises a shortfall, and the centre answers
detail: Three smaller incoherences on the shortfall record. (1) The magnitude is not reconstructable: Kukawa's 94 is (weekly_burn x 2) - stock_on_hand (tab_partner.jsx:341-344), but neither the two-week horizon nor the weekly burn appears on the card or in the modal, and the modal's Children affected / Cartons short rows carry no hint while its Needed by row does. A viewer sees 94 with no way to derive it — and 94 also appears elsewhere on the page as Askira's inbound consignment, inviting a misread. (2) CARTONS SHORT and CHILDREN AFFECTED render as two identical adjacent numeric columns with no differentiating treatment and no definition on the card; the carton-to-child rule exists only as ~11px grey text in another card's footnote, so the pair reads as a duplicated column rather than a stated conversion. (3) The seeded Askira signal's needed_by is TODAY+7 = Aug 4 (demo/demand.py:481) while Askira's own cover row says it runs dry Aug 1 — a deadline three days after the site is already empty. The live Kukawa raise is correct here, since the modal prefills needed_by from stockout_on.
fix_recommendation: Add a derivation hint under Cartons short in the modal ('two weeks of cover at this site's burn rate, less what it is holding') and on the card, consistent with the app's own stated principle that every figure carries its method. Render CHILDREN AFFECTED as '94 children' with an info bubble on the header carrying the one-carton-per-full-course rule inline on this card. Seed the Askira signal's needed_by from its stockout_on rather than a fixed TODAY+7 offset.
